transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 62 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Asha Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Leah Chen (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Aureus ML Platform Lead), Priya Singh (Aureus CTO), Marco Lopez (Aureus Infra)
-- Auto-summary (auto-generated): deep dive on model-specific tuning for Llama/Mistral/Qwen with emphasis on MoE and RoPE behavior; action items to run benchmarks and share security docs.

00:00 - Asha: alright everyone, thanks for joining. good to see y'all. we wanted to do a focused deep-dive on the architecture-specific tuning bits you asked about — llama, mistral, and qwen, plus moe routing costs and rope scaling. is that still the right scope?
00:18 - Daniel: yeah that's perfect, thanks. we had a few incidents with long-context drift and higher tail latency under bursts so want to understand root causes.
00:30 - Marco R: great. quick note — apologies in advance, my mic is a little noisy. so i'll jump into MoE first since priya flagged routing overhead as a blocker for on-prem.
00:45 - Priya: yep, routing CPU overhead is our worry — if moe routing doubles infra, finance will flag it.
00:58 - Marco R: right, so MoE (or M-O-E) models bring big capacity wins but routing isn't free. you pay memory for expert params plus per-request dispatch overhead. in our runtime we do batched routing to amortize that but there are two costs: 1) increased host->device dispatch for expert indices, 2) load imbalance when gating picks small subset of experts and causes hotspotting.
01:20 - Marco R: in practice, for a 8-expert moe layer, if gating isn't temperature-tuned you can get 2x-3x tail latency at small batch sizes. the fix is: better gating (top-k with soft penalty), dynamic routing batch coalescing, and per-expert rate limiters.
01:42 - Daniel: are these fixes config only or do they need kernel changes?
01:50 - Marco R: mostly orchestrator changes and some batching heuristics. kernel-level changes only for extremely hot experts where you might want fused expert kernels. we can try to emulate in Dedicated without kernel dev first.
02:05 - Priya: ok. next, rope — we've seen hallucinations and context decay after ~8k tokens. is that expected?
02:12 - Leah: so RoPE (rope, sometimes transcribed rowp) is position encoding that can degrade past certain base freq. models like llama2, older qwen versions use standard rope and you'll see phase mismatch for very long sequences. two tactical options: rope scaling (linear or dynamic), ALiBi style biasing, or position interpolation during compilation.
02:36 - Marco R: short version: rope scaling (we've implemented a few variants) often reduces decay but can interact badly with quantization. need to run cross-checks.
02:48 - Daniel: do you have examples? we have sample prompts up to 40k tokens for a document retrieval pipeline.
02:55 - Marco R: okay that's great — we'll run a long-context pass; quick note though, qwen-family has different RoPE internals and may actually behave better out-of-box for some patterns; mistral has aggressive rotary parametrization which can be tuned too.
03:12 - Priya: so for our scoring pipeline, what's the immediate recommendation?
03:18 - Marco R: start with rope-scaling + KV cache prefetching. keep sequence lenses clipped for generation and use prefix caching for retrieval. for evals we'll run few long-context end-to-end runs to measure perplexity drift and token-level accuracy.
03:32 - Marco L: can KV cache be shared across user sessions to reduce cold-starts?
03:38 - Leah: yes but with caveats — shared KV cache helps for repeated prefixes, but you'll need robust eviction; we provide policies: LRU, size-based, and time-decay. watch memory fragmentation on GPU when you evict large KV kv-chunks.
03:58 - Daniel: any rough numbers on memory overhead for kv per request?
04:05 - Marco R: depends on seqlen and hidden dim — ballpark for 70B models: ~1.2-1.6MB per token in uncompressed float16 KV; with quantized KV (packed) we get down to ~0.4-0.6MB per token. using prefix cache you can amortize across requests.
04:28 - Priya: that helps. about quant — which profile do you recommend? nf4 vs 4-bit vs gptq?
04:35 - Marco R: nf4/GPTQ combos are our current sweet spots. nf4 with symmetric quant for activations + GPTQ for weights tends to keep quality high while reducing memory. 4-bit naive often regresses on Mistral unless you apply per-channel scales. we saw Mistral-70B with GPTQ+nf4 get within 1-2% of baseline on common evals.
05:02 - Daniel: and kernel support? will runtime pick optimized kernels?
05:07 - Marco R: the compilation layer selects kernels based on model archetype, quant type, and sequence distribution. for nf4 we use special int8/int4 GEMM kernels; if not available fallback to semi-optimized paths which cost some latency. we'll log that in the perf sheet.
05:25 - Priya: mention of kernels makes me ask about batching — we're sensitive to p95 latency under 300ms. how do you tune batch sizes while staying under that SLO?
05:36 - Marco R: two levers: max batch size and dynamic batching window. for low-latency SLOs we keep window small (~10-20ms) and use hot-path kernels for common seqlens. also prioritize shorter requests in the scheduler (latency-first). we can set multi-tier queues so critical endpoints get lower batching delay.
06:00 - Daniel: can you share the scheduling config for that?
06:03 - Asha: yes we'll share a recommended config in the perf spreadsheet.
06:08 - Marco R: also watch KV cache interaction — heavy prefix cache hits reduce computation, enabling bigger batches without breaking latency SLOs. but cache miss storms will cause latency spikes. we actively monitor cache hit rates in the console.
06:22 - Marco L: on-prem concerns: we need KMS/HSM for key material and private control plane. what's Redwood's approach?
06:30 - Leah: for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, or HSMs on prem. control plane can be configured to run in a customer VPC or as air-gapped with a small bootstrap channel. audit logs are retained and fed to your SIEM. we'll send a checklist.
06:47 - Priya: great. any known gotchas with HSM latencies on the critical path?
06:52 - Leah: generally we keep KMS calls off the hot path. HSM is used for key unwrap/wrap of model keys at startup; we cache the unwrapped keys in memory and rotate per policy. only rotation ops hit the HSM.
07:07 - Daniel: back to MoE — do you have cost numbers to show infra delta vs dense baseline?
07:13 - Marco R: rough rule: MoE can reduce FLOPs per token by 2-3x (because only subset of experts run) but parameter storage goes up. in our Dedicated tests, for bursty traffic MoE latency tail can be 1.5-2x unless you tweak routing or overprovision experts. net cost depends on request distribution — for steady high-throughput it's often cheaper; for spiky low-QPS it's worse.
07:41 - Priya: are you able to fallback to dense variants automatically?
07:45 - Marco R: yes, Smart routing can fallback to dense-compatible checkpoints; we do model variants pinning. for the pilot we can capture metrics and auto-fallback on latency/p95 breach.
07:56 - Priya: ok perfect. any specific tuning for Qwen? we've seen mixed behavior on long context.
08:04 - Marco R: Qwen tends to have different RoPE frequency choices and some tokenization differences. quantization-wise Qwen is a bit more sensitive to per-channel scale; we recommend per-tensor+per-channel hybrid GPTQ. we'll include a recommended config for Qwen in the spreadsheet.
08:20 - Daniel: awesome. how do we validate quality regressions after quant? we need guardrails for production.
08:25 - Marco R: use unit eval prompts + regression harness. Redwood Optimize ties eval alerts to prompt sets and can trigger rollback if quality drops beyond threshold. for the pilot we'll set a small suite of 200 prompts you provide.
08:40 - Priya: ok we'll send the prompts.
08:43 - Marco R: great. also want to call out weirdness: rope scaling + quantization sometimes interacts and causes oscillation in logits for some tokens; that's why we test combined changes not isolated.
08:57 - Daniel: got it. what about tooling to visualize KV caches and expert loads?
09:02 - Leah: Console shows per-route KV hit rate, per-expert QPS and memory footprint. we can also export traces for perf debug.
09:12 - Marco L: is there any plan to open-source tuning scripts?
09:16 - Asha: we have community notebooks and some scripts—will share links; core runtime is not OSS though.
09:23 - Daniel: we talked about benchmarks — what's the baseline test you want us to run on our side vs what Redwood will run?
09:30 - Marco R: good question. we suggest a two-step: 1) Redwood runs baseline on Dedicated staging with our standard kernels and your sample prompts (we'll run Llama2-70B (nf4/gptq), Mistral-70B (4-bit/per-channel), Qwen-70B (hybrid)) for 1k and 10k contexts; 2) Aureus runs a short on-prem run (if possible) with a lightweight harness to validate environment parity. we'll capture p50/p90/p95 latencies, throughput (tokens/sec), KV hit rates, and memory.
10:03 - Priya: timeline?
10:06 - Asha: we'll prep the perf sheet today, Marco R will run the staging tests this week, expected artifacts by 2026-03-10.
10:12 - Daniel: good. on the security docs, we need SOC2 plus data residency note.
10:16 - Asha: will send SOC2/ISO and data residency details.
10:20 - Marco R: one more perf note — when you enable aggressive batching to save cost, tail latency can blow up on cache-miss storms. we recommend progressive rollout: start with conservative batching and enable autoscale/burst for non-critical routes.
10:36 - Priya: makes sense. anything else on RoPE math? are there parameters (scale factor) you recommend to try first?
10:42 - Marco R: yes, try base scale 1.25 and also a progressive schedule that increases scale for tokens > 4k. we'll include scripts for applying scale and running small evals.
10:55 - Daniel: how invasive is that to the checkpoint? need to re-finetune?
10:59 - Marco R: usually no full finetune. minor interpolation or scaling is often fine; in worst cases a lightweight calibration step helps. we'll document per-model guidance.
11:12 - Leah: ops note for on-prem: ensure your GPU drivers match our recommended stack, and that you provide device memory headroom — quant helps but you still need 10-20% spare for transient KV peaks.
11:28 - Marco L: noted. any limitations around H100 vs A100?
11:33 - Marco R: H100 gives better fp16 & sparse throughput for big models; A100 is fine with right kernel paths. we'll call out differences in the perf sheet.
11:45 - Priya: ok, can we get a cost model? rough delta between hosted vs dedicated vs private?
11:50 - Asha: yes we'll include a cost-estimator spreadsheet showing per-token cost with different batch/quant settings and expected infra commit for Dedicated.
11:59 - Daniel: perfect. last question — for MoE, if we want to avoid hotspots can we limit expert selection to a fixed subset?
12:06 - Marco R: yes you can force expert routing masks or balanced top-k gating; that's a good short-term mitigation but reduces model capacity. again tradeoff chart in the sheet.
12:20 - Priya: sounds good.
12:22 - Asha: ok let's recap next steps — Marco R runs the benchmarks and shares logs, Leah shares VPC/KMS checklist, Asha shares perf/price sheet and SOC2 docs, Daniel provides prompts and sample load patterns. we'll target follow-up call after results.
12:42 - Daniel: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
12:45 - Priya: thanks.
12:47 - Marco L: thanks all.
12:50 - Asha: thanks, talk soon.
-- End transcript (note: some words auto-transcribed imperfectly, e.g., "rope" as "rowp", product names occasionally mis-capitalized).
